title: Precision hunt — field notes and quick repros
content:
Purpose: quick personal scratchpad while triaging a production regression where intermittent NaNs appear in token outputs when serving certain fp8-quantized models (sparse-attn variant).

Session summary (short):
- Repro: ~1 in 20 requests for sequence length 2048 produces a NaN token and causes client-visible truncation.
- Affected model variants: modelX-small-fp8-q4 (per-channel scales) + specialized sparse attention kernel.
- Not affected: same model in bf16 mode, and the non-sparse attention build.

What I ran (commands and env):
- baseline reproduce (inside docker image: redwood/inference:canary-2025-10-19)
  export OMP_NUM_THREADS=2
  export NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1
  python -u tests/repro/random_request_runner.py --model modelX-small-fp8-q4 --seqlen 2048 --batch 1 --requests 500 --seed 1337

- attempted variations quickly:
  # disable cublasLt fused kernel fallback
  CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 python -u tests/repro/random_request_runner.py ...
  # run without sparse-attn optimized kernel
  python -u tests/repro/random_request_runner.py --kernel standard_attn --model modelX-small-fp8-q4
  # run in bf16 to show baseline stability
  python -u tests/repro/random_request_runner.py --dtype bf16 --model modelX-small-bf16

Observed error snippets (copied from stdout/stderr):
- generation worker log (truncated):
  INFO:serve: request id 0x7f3a... started
  WARNING:inference.kv_cache: kv cache miss at layer 8
  ERROR:inference.runtime: output token NaN at step 211 (logits contain NaN)
  Traceback (most recent recent frame removed)
  RuntimeError: NaN encountered in softmax at layer 8, device: cuda:0
  
- cuda kernel trace (narrow):
  [W] smallpt: detected inf in kernel fast_scale_apply
  [E] triton: kernel fusion produced NaN in block 32

What I tried and quick results (notes):
- seed fixing (seed 1337) 
  -> no correlation: still intermittent under fixed seed (different failure points across runs), suggests non-determinism from kernels / memory race.

- force deterministic cuDNN + disable JIT compile
  export TORCH_USE_CUDA_DSA=0
  export PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:64
  python -u ...  -> failure rate dropped from ~5% to ~1.8% (improved but not solved).

- change layernorm eps
  # quick instrumented patch in model_impl.py: LayerNorm(eps=1e-5) -> LayerNorm(eps=1e-3)
  -> immediate reduction in NaNs (failures ~0.2% in 1000 requests). Hypothesis: quantization + reduced dynamic range caused denom underflow/very large scale in per-channel scales after quant.

- clamp logits before softmax (temporary mitigation)
  logits = torch.clamp(logits, min=-1e4, max=1e4)
  -> no NaNs observed in 2000 requests. This is a mitigation, not root cause.

- disabling sparse-attention kernel and using fallback
  -> completely eliminated NaNs in 5000 requests. Strong indicator that sparse-attn kernel's fused ops + quant handling produce instability under certain patterns.

Minimal repro (python) I used to stress local container (paste):

```
import torch
from model_impl import ModelX
m = ModelX.from_pretrained('modelX-small-fp8-q4')
torch.manual_seed(1337)
seq = torch.randint(0, m.vocab_size, (1, 2048), device='cuda')
for i in range(1000):
    out = m.forward(seq)
    if torch.isnan(out.logits).any():
        print('NaN at iter', i)
        break
```

(Notes: added fast path to print layer-wise stats, found NaN usually shows up after cross-attention in layer 7-9.)

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Sparse-attn fused kernel incorrectly handles subnormal/denorm floats after quant-dequant roundtrip when per-channel scale is tiny — leads to large divide in attention normalization.
2) Tiny eps in LayerNorm -> when combined with quantization scale quant rounding to 0 for small channels, denom underflow produces huge scale before softmax.
3) Triton kernel race with shared memory not zeroed between warps under specific sequence patterns; random but reproducible with the sparseness pattern of tokens.
4) Bitsandbytes-style fake-quant vs runtime fused dequantization mismatch (scale placement) for INT8/FP8 hybrid path.

Quick instrumentation I added (and why):
- per-layer min/max stats for activations (float32 keep) before and after quant/dequant.
- track counts of subnormal values (abs(x) < 1e-38) in activation tensors.
- toggles to enable/disable stochastic rounding when dequantizing (AB quant library).

Key findings from instrumentation:
- Layers that later produce NaN often show a burst of subnormals in the pre-activated keys/queries (layer 7).
- When stochastic rounding ON, subnormal count increases (weird), and NaN incidence is slightly lower — suggests rounding behavior matters.

Short-term mitigations pushed to canary (sketch):
- increase LayerNorm eps to 1e-3 in quantized model pack (safe regression tests).
- clamp logits at inference runtime (cheap) while we root-cause.
- route suspect customers away from sparse-attn kernel (policy-based routing) until kernel fix.

Next steps (practical list):
- [ ] Add unit test that simulates sparse token patterns that historically triggered NaN (need to extract from logs). Ticket: JIRA-ENG-1987.
- [ ] PR to add per-layer eps override in model config so customers using quant packs can tune eps without model re-export.
- [ ] File bug with triton team: include minimal C-level repro captured from kernel trace + env. Reach out to @Jonah for kernel binary + logs.
- [ ] Try reproducing on AMD ROCm machines (check whether it's CUDA-only); set up a 2-GPU ROCm node for a 48h stress run.
- [ ] Experiment with per-channel scale floor (force min scale 1e-3) at quantization time and run 10k requests.

Notes-to-self / friction points observed:
- local dev image uses older triton (2.0.x) while canary uses 2.3.x; kernel behavior differs. Need to standardize test infra.
- stack traces scrubbed of memory addresses in production logs; keep a private copy of a full dump for kernel teams.
- turning determinism on reduces noise but can hide race conditions; run both deterministic and non.

Useful commands/quick helpers I added to repro scripts:
- filter logs for NaNs: rg "NaN encountered|output token NaN" -n 
- capture cublas/cuDNN kernel calls: nvprof --profile-from-start off --log-file kernel.txt python -u ... (slow)

Random notes / loose ideas:
- test forcing denormals to flush to zero at CUDA driver/env level (may mask issue but interesting): https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-runtime-api/group__CUDART__ENV.html
- consider switching per-channel -> per-tensor scales for extremely small channels as pragmatic fallback during quantization.
- could be exacerbated by KV cache reuse across requests (memory not cleared fully). Check kv_cache.clear() path.

My current working hypothesis: combination of tiny per-channel scales + low-layernorm-eps + fused sparse-attn kernel that assumes no subnormals leads to ephemeral infinities which then propagate through softmax. Kernel fix or defensively clamping/eps increase will resolve.

If you pick this up: start by reproducing with the fallback attn kernel disabled/enabled to confirm, then try the per-channel scale floor experiment (quick to implement at export time).

-- Aisha
